cognitive_validation.rationale: The dog's behavior is presented in a coherent, naturalistic, nonsupernatural manner (homing instinct, trained commands, physiological description of the pre-howl), but coherence alone does not create a novum absent a world-altering difference.

novum_candidates.description: A part-wolf sled dog ('Wolf'/'Brown') is given a genuine choice between two masters and two lives (pastoral California vs. harsh Klondike), and his autonomous decision resolves the story.
novum_candidates.estrangement_rationale: The proof-of-ownership by sled commands provides a mild reader-facing contrast between domestic and frontier worlds, but produces recognition, not cognitive estrangement from an empirical norm.

narrative_hegemony.rationale: The dog's identity and ultimate choice do drive the entire narrative logic, but centrality of a mundane element does not make it a novum.

novelty.rationale: Nothing in the story alters the empirical norm. A trained sled dog obeying driving commands, howling, and choosing to follow a former owner are all ordinary canine behaviors within the real world. There is no totalizing world-altering difference from the author's empirical reality; the setting is turn-of-the-century California and the Klondike as they actually were.
